name: Rosemary hair oil

card.summary: A scalp and hair oil based on rosemary, used by people who want to support thicker-looking hair and a healthier scalp, often as a gentler add-on to other hair routines.
card.aka: rosemary oil for hair, Rosmarinus officinalis oil
card.note: Essential oils can irritate skin and should be diluted; no standard formulation exists.

quick.overview:
Rosemary hair oil is a scalp and hair product made with rosemary, either as an essential oil blended into a carrier oil or as an infused oil. Rosemary oil has long been used in perfumery and personal care; the historical Hungary water was largely distilled rosemary [1].

The appearance payoff users cite is fuller-looking hair and a healthier scalp. A 2025 network meta-analysis estimated relative efficacy of topical rosemary oil alongside conventional treatments, while a 2025 Canadian expert panel did not recommend it among 45 interventions reviewed [2].
quick.how: People massage a diluted rosemary oil into the scalp, often alongside other hair-care steps, and users describe judging results over several months.
quick.risks: Essential oils can cause scalp irritation or allergic reactions, which is why products are formulated in carrier oils. Camphor makes up a large share of rosemary oil [1].

lead: Rosemary hair oil is a topical scalp product based on rosemary, a Mediterranean herb whose essential oil contains around 150 compounds including camphor and carnosic acid [1]. It is sold as a ready-made oil or mixed by users from rosemary essential oil and a carrier.

People use it to care for the scalp and to try to maintain hair density. The reasons given include its traditional status as a hair and fragrance ingredient and interest in plant-based alternatives to drug treatments.

Published assessments include a 2025 network meta-analysis of 24 trials that estimated efficacy for topical rosemary oil relative to conventional treatments, and a 2025 Canadian consensus whose panel of 11 physicians did not recommend rosemary oil among interventions reviewed [2].

chain: Reported effect on scalp and follicle environment
angle.text: Users apply the oil to the scalp hoping to maintain density or support growth. It is used as a gentle addition rather than a replacement for medical treatment.

paras: Rosemary is used in perfumes, shampoos and aromatherapy, and its extract is a food preservative (E392) [1]. Hair oils combine it with carrier oils so it can be applied to the scalp.

A 2025 network meta-analysis of 24 trials gave relative efficacy estimates for topical rosemary oil among over-the-counter products compared with conventional treatments [2]. A 2025 Canadian Delphi consensus did not recommend rosemary oil [2]. No formulation-specific trial of rosemary hair oil blends was found.
